# `canair wican`

```
usage: canair wican [-h] <command> ...

[UDS] Build and sync the WiCAN device's AutoPID profile.

Nothing is written until you ask for it — a bare `canair wican` prints this help. Choose a subcommand:
  autopid write     generate the v4 and v6 AutoPID JSON to the bundle's out/
  autopid upload    generate + upload to the device (Pro)
  autopid download  download the device's current AutoPID JSON (Pro)
  autopid diff      download + diff against the generated JSON (Pro)
  autopid show      print the generated JSON for a QUERY, offline
  autopid stats     per-ECU/PID statistics table
  mode show         show the device's active protocol
  mode set MODE     switch the device protocol/mode, reboot + align transport (Pro)

positional arguments:
  <command>
    autopid   Generate/sync the WiCAN AutoPID profile JSON
    mode      Show or set the WiCAN device protocol/mode

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

Build and sync the WiCAN device's AutoPID vehicle profile.

`canair wican` groups two families of device operations. Nothing is written
until you ask for it — a bare `canair wican` just prints this help.

Terminology (deliberately disambiguated):
  * the canair *profile bundle* — the `profiles/<name>/` directory (ecus/,
    profile.yaml, captures/, …) managed by `canair profile`; and
  * the WiCAN *AutoPID profile* — the JSON generated from that bundle's
    ecus/ and stored on the device's AutoPID feature, managed here.

Subcommands:
  autopid write               Generate the v4 and v6 AutoPID JSON to the bundle's out/
  autopid upload              Generate + upload to the device (Pro only)
  autopid download            Download the device's current AutoPID JSON (Pro)
  autopid diff                Download + diff against the generated JSON (Pro)
  autopid show [QUERY]        Print the generated JSON for some PIDs (offline)
  autopid stats               Per-ECU/PID statistics table
  mode show                   Show the device's active protocol
  mode set MODE               Switch the device protocol/mode + align transport (Pro)

Examples:
  canair wican autopid write                       # verified-only, both firmware files
  canair wican autopid write --firmware 6          # only the firmware v6 table
  canair wican autopid write --include-unverified  # also unverified: autopid-v*-unverified.json
  canair wican autopid write --no-expected-responses  # omit the response-frame counts
  canair wican autopid upload --reboot             # upload + reboot to apply
  canair wican autopid diff --wican home           # compare device vs generated
  canair wican autopid show BMS:2101 --firmware 6  # what one PID ships as
  canair wican mode set slcan                 # raw CAN + set transport slcan-tcp
```

## `canair wican autopid`

```
usage: canair wican autopid [-h] <action> ...

Build the WiCAN AutoPID profile from the active bundle's ecus/ and (optionally) sync it with the device.

positional arguments:
  <action>
    write     Generate the AutoPID JSON for firmware 4.x and v6 to the
              bundle's out/
    upload    Generate + upload the AutoPID profile to the device (Pro)
    download  Download the device's current AutoPID profile (Pro)
    diff      Download + diff the device profile against the generated one
              (Pro)
    show      Print the AutoPID JSON that write would generate, for the PIDs a
              QUERY selects
    stats     Show a per-ECU/PID statistics table

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `canair wican autopid write`

```
usage: canair wican autopid write [-h] [--firmware {4,6}] [--out PATH]
                                  [--include-unverified]
                                  [--no-expected-responses]

Generate the WiCAN AutoPID profile and write it to the active bundle's out/,
once per firmware generation: autopid-v4.json is the 4.x vehicle profile,
autopid-v6.json the v6 AutoPID table (from 6.0.0-beta.3; it also names the
car's 'vehicle' and 'specific_init' device settings). On a profile with
several variants both go to out/<variant>/, one device profile per car. With
--include-unverified they are autopid-v4-unverified.json and
autopid-v6-unverified.json instead, so the verified-only files stay as they
are. Refused while an ECU's revision is undetermined: the device polls a fixed
list and can't detect it.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --firmware {4,6}      Write only the file for this WiCAN firmware generation
                        (default: both)
  --out PATH            Write to PATH instead of the bundle's out/ (needs
                        --firmware: one file)
  --include-unverified  Include unverified parameters (default: verified only)
  --no-expected-responses
                        Do not append each PID's recorded response_frames
                        count to its request (by default the count is
                        appended, so the adapter answers as soon as that many
                        frames arrive instead of waiting out its ~614ms
                        budget)
```

### `canair wican autopid upload`

```
usage: canair wican autopid upload [-h] [--reboot] [--include-unverified]
                                   [--no-expected-responses] [--wican WICAN]
                                   [--no-fallback]

Generate the AutoPID profile and upload it to the WiCAN device (POST
/store_car_data). WiCAN Pro on firmware 4.x only.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --reboot              Reboot the device after upload
  --include-unverified  Include unverified parameters (default: verified only)
  --no-expected-responses
                        Do not append each PID's recorded response_frames
                        count to its request (by default the count is
                        appended, so the adapter answers as soon as that many
                        frames arrive instead of waiting out its ~614ms
                        budget)
  --wican WICAN         WiCAN address: ap, an IP/host, or a URL (default:
                        config transport.host / default_wican=ap, falling back
                        to another configured device when it is unreachable)
  --no-fallback         Don't fall back to another configured device when the
                        default is unreachable (see config transport.fallback)
```

```
usage: canair wican autopid download [-h] [--wican WICAN] [--no-fallback]

only.

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --wican WICAN  WiCAN address: ap, an IP/host, or a URL (default: config
                 transport.host / default_wican=ap, falling back to another

  --no-fallback  Don't fall back to another configured device when the default

```

### `canair wican autopid show`

```
usage: canair wican autopid show [-h] [--firmware {4,6}]
                                 [--include-unverified]
                                 [--no-expected-responses]
                                 [QUERY ...]

Generate the AutoPID profile in memory and print it as one JSON document,
{"v4": …, "v6": …}, narrowed to the PIDs the QUERY selects. Reads ecus/, never
out/, and writes nothing. The progress lines go to stderr. The smallest way to
check what one PID ships as.

positional arguments:
  QUERY                 ECU/PID selection, e.g. 'BMS:2101' or 'VCU' (default:
                        every shipped PID)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --firmware {4,6}      Print only this WiCAN firmware generation's document
                        (default: both)
  --include-unverified  Include unverified parameters (default: verified only)
  --no-expected-responses
                        Do not append each PID's recorded response_frames
                        count to its request (by default the count is
                        appended, so the adapter answers as soon as that many
                        frames arrive instead of waiting out its ~614ms
                        budget)
```

## `canair wican mode`

```
usage: canair wican mode [-h] <action> ...

Inspect or switch the WiCAN device's operating protocol (elm327/slcan/auto_pid/…). This is the device's own mode, distinct from the AutoPID profile. Firmware 4.x only: v6 has no protocol mode.

positional arguments:
  <action>
    show      Show the device's active protocol
    set       Switch the device protocol/mode and reboot (Pro)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `canair wican mode show`

```
usage: canair wican mode show [-h] [--wican WICAN] [--no-fallback]

Report the WiCAN device's currently active protocol/mode.

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --wican WICAN  WiCAN address: ap, an IP/host, or a URL (default: config
                 transport.host / default_wican=ap, falling back to another
                 configured device when it is unreachable)
  --no-fallback  Don't fall back to another configured device when the default
                 is unreachable (see config transport.fallback)
```

### `canair wican mode set`

```
usage: canair wican mode set [-h] [--yes] [--no-transport] [--wican WICAN]
                             [--no-fallback]
                             {elm327,slcan,savvycan,realdash66,auto_pid}

Switch the WiCAN device to MODE and reboot it, then align canair's transport to match (slcan -> slcan-tcp, elm327 -> wican-ws). WiCAN Pro on firmware 4.x only.

Valid modes:
  slcan        raw CAN — canair drives ISO-TP client-side; enables sniff
  elm327       ELM327 terminal — the dongle runs ISO-TP
  auto_pid     restore Home Assistant AutoPID broadcasting
  savvycan     stream frames to SavvyCAN
  realdash66   stream frames to RealDash (CAN 66)

positional arguments:
  {elm327,slcan,savvycan,realdash66,auto_pid}
                        Target protocol/mode

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --yes                 Skip the confirmation prompt
  --no-transport        Don't auto-align the config transport.type to the new
                        mode
  --wican WICAN         WiCAN address: ap, an IP/host, or a URL (default:
                        config transport.host / default_wican=ap, falling back
                        to another configured device when it is unreachable)
  --no-fallback         Don't fall back to another configured device when the
                        default is unreachable (see config transport.fallback)
```
